verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y wins, narrowly but on verified substance. The brief explicitly demands that every in-repo line citation of this machinery be checked; Y found and verified ~14 stale citations against X's ~6, including two the key scores (K17 hooks/goal-inert-watch.sh:36 citing 4671-4688, and M7 docs/plans/NONLIMIT_RESUME_LADDER.md:753 citing :4994-5009) plus four the key does not (handoff-fire.sh:6942→:5686, :12358→:4828/4844/4861, LIVENESS_DETECTOR_FAILNEG.md:208→:3574, A05:106→:12406-12412, and the file's own set -euo pipefail self-citations '(:273)'/'(:197)' against the real :343). I opened all of these and every one resolves as Y describes. Y also refutes CLAUDE.global.md:224's 'a refusal is printed, never silent', which is exactly the brief's item-6 readership question. X is not weak — it has zero bad citations I could find and three genuine unique finds (the `shell)` early-return at :12441-12446 that skips inheritance entirely and that neither other output noticed; the superseded in-file claim at :5707; the transcript_for_sid `*/*` guard contrast at :4679/:4682) — but Y's key coverage is 25/25 against X's 23/25 and its only defects are one mis-pointed supporting citation (:12646 for the /exit, which is at :12725) and a one-block-off test range.

X vs Z — X wins on a specific, verified, material difference: item 6 asks where the refusal is announced and WHO CAN ACTUALLY READ IT. X answers correctly (foreground process's stderr = the predecessor's own Bash tool, which the typed /exit kills — quoting :12509-12511, and detach at :1696-1697 redirects only the watcher's streams, so neither the watcher log nor the successor ever sees it). Z answers 'visible to whoever is watching that pane at that moment' and calls the lines 'pane-local', which is the optimistic reading the script's own comment and tests/handoff-goal-arm.bats:400-405 contradict. X additionally found the second skip branch at :12441-12446 (verified) that Z missed while both cover the resume branch. Key coverage is tied at 23/25, and Z's unique wins (the :12796 resume summary line, the goal_armed_for_pane disambiguation, the fail-open/fail-closed framing) do not offset a wrong answer to an explicitly asked sub-question plus two loose citation ranges (cc_sid_for_pane 'defined 4955-4989' truncates at :4998; the :5780-5786 rationale belongs to a different function).

Y vs Z — Y wins on both axes. Key coverage 25/25 vs 23/25 (Z misses K17 and M7), Y's stale-citation sweep is roughly triple Z's and every entry I opened holds, and Y answers the readership question correctly where Z asserts the wrong direction. Z's verbatim quoting is genuinely good practice and its :12796 find is real, but Y independently covers the resume skip with the same code-level certainty and adds the FIRE_GOAL assignment census (verified: :508, :5847, :5852, :7158, :8950, :12538 and nothing else) that turns the 'exported FIRE_GOAL is the only other trip' claim from assertion into proof.
